module_title: Autobiographies of Famous Personalities - Foundational (Sports & Politics)
introduction: Autobiographies are one of the most heavily tested topics in the 'Books and Authors' section of Static GK. At this foundational level, we focus on the most iconic Indian leaders and legendary athletes whose autobiographies appear repeatedly in SSC, Railways, and state-level exams.

core_concepts.title: Wings of Fire
core_concepts.description: The highly inspiring autobiography of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, the 11th President of India and the 'Missile Man'. It details his early life, struggles, and his role in the development of India's space and missile programs.

core_concepts.title: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
core_concepts.description: The autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi. Originally written in Gujarati, it covers his life from early childhood through to 1921, detailing his spiritual and political evolution.

core_concepts.title: Playing It My Way
core_concepts.description: The autobiography of Sachin Tendulkar, famously known as the 'God of Cricket'. It chronicles his legendary 24-year-long international cricket career, personal struggles, and monumental achievements.

core_concepts.title: The Race of My Life
core_concepts.description: The autobiography of the legendary Indian sprinter Milkha Singh, popularly known as the 'Flying Sikh'. The famous Bollywood biopic 'Bhaag Milkha Bhaag' was directly based on this book.

important_entities.name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
important_entities.key_fact: Book: Wings of Fire (Co-authored with Arun Tiwari)
important_entities.significance: Pivotal scientist behind India's Agni and Prithvi missiles.

important_entities.name: Mahatma Gandhi
important_entities.key_fact: Book: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
important_entities.significance: The primary leader of India's independence movement; pioneered Satyagraha.

important_entities.name: Sachin Tendulkar
important_entities.significance: The only player in cricket history to score 100 international centuries.

important_entities.name: Milkha Singh
important_entities.key_fact: Book: The Race of My Life
important_entities.significance: The first Indian athlete to win an individual athletics gold medal at the Commonwealth Games (1958).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Aspirants frequently confuse the autobiographies of Milkha Singh and Yuvraj Singh. Milkha Singh was a runner, hence his book is 'The RACE of My Life'. Yuvraj Singh battled cancer (a major test), so his book is 'The TEST of My Life'.
Exams often ask for the original language of 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth'. It was NOT English; it was originally serialized and written in Gujarati.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Milkha runs the Race, Yuvraj passes the Test
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Race = Milkha Singh. Test (of Cancer/Life) = Yuvraj Singh.
Missile Man = APJ Abdul Kalam = Wings of Fire.

exam_strategy_tips: Cricketers' autobiographies are the most heavily targeted area in SSC exams. Memorize the books of Sachin, Sourav Ganguly, and Kapil Dev as a priority.
